'''''Bambusa oldhamii''''', known as '''giant timber bamboo''' or '''Oldham's bamboo''', is a large species of [[bamboo]]. It is the most common and widely grown bamboo in the [[United States]] and has been introduced into cultivation around the world. It is densely foliated, growing up to {{convert|20|m|ft|round=5|abbr=off}} tall in good conditions, and can have a diameter of up to {{convert|10|cm|in|0|abbr=off}}.

==Description==
''Bambusa oldhamii'' grows to {{convert|17|-|20|m|ft|abbr=on|0}} in height, with green [[culm (botany)|culms]] reaching a maximum of {{convert|10|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} in diameter.<ref name="orhn99">{{cite book|last=Ohrnberger|first=Dieter|title=The Bamboos of the World|url=https://archive.org/details/bamboosworld00ohrn|url-access=limited|publisher=Elsevier|location=Amsterdam|date=1999|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bamboosworld00ohrn/page/n269 271]–72|isbn=0-444-50020-0}}</ref> Shoots grow rapidly in warmer months. The branches are short and leaves long.<ref name=Mered01>{{cite book|last=Meredith|first=Ted|title=Bamboo for gardens|publisher=Timber Press|date=2001|pages=251–52|isbn=0-88192-507-1}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
It was first described by Munro in 1868, the [[type specimen]] collected in Taiwan by Richard Oldham (after whom the species was named). It is grouped in the subgenus ''Dendrocalamopsis''. ''Dendrocalamus latiflorus'' is a misapplied name, under which it has been sold in the United States. It has also been confused with the related species ''B. atrovirens'' of [[Zhejiang]] in mainland China.<ref name="orhn99"/><!-- this ref cites whole para -->

==Distribution and habitat==
''B. oldhamii'' is native to the island of [[Taiwan]] and to southern [[China]] ([[Fujian]], [[Guangdong]], [[Guangxi]], [[Hainan]], [[Zhejiang]]). It is widely cultivated and has become naturalized in several places ([[Ryukyu Islands]], [[New Zealand]], [[Chiapas]], [[Honduras]], [[Peru]], etc.)<ref name=m>{{Cite web|url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=398934|title = World Checklist of Selected Plant Families: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew}}</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242307677 Flora of China Vol. 22 Page 36, <big>绿竹</big> lü zhu, ''Bambusa oldhamii'' Munro, Trans. ==Cultivation==
It has been introduced into cultivation around the world; it is grown under glass in [[Germany]],<ref name="orhn99"/> and in [[Australia]], [[Puerto Rico]], [[Florida]], [[Texas]], [[Tennessee]], [[Maryland]], [[Virginia]], [[North Carolina]], [[South Carolina]], [[Oklahoma]], [[Kentucky]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], [[Alabama]], [[Arkansas]], [[Mississippi]], [[Arizona]], [[Nevada]], [[Hawaii]], [[Louisiana]], and [[California]], where it is the most common clumping bamboo grown.<ref name="orhn99"/> The maximum height in cultivation varies with the temperature. It tolerates temperatures down to −7 °C (19 °F).<ref name=Mered01/>

In [[Taiwan]] and China, [[bamboo shoot|the young shoots]] of ''B. oldhamii'' are highly sought after due to their crisp texture and sweet taste.<ref name="tw">{{citation |title=香筍入菜 |publisher=行政院農業委員會 |url=http://kmweb.coa.gov.tw/subject/ct.asp?xItem=1022255&ctNode=3692&mp=263&kpi=0&hashid= |access-date=2015-08-12 |archive-date=2016-10-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006051606/http://kmweb.coa.gov.tw/subject/ct.asp?xItem=1022255&ctNode=3692&mp=263&kpi=0&hashid= |url-status=dead }}</ref> Cultivation in Taiwan has declined with many stands of bamboo [[Pineapple production in Taiwan|converted to pineapple production]], a number of subsidy and support programs have been established as the cultivated bamboo groves provide valuable wildlife habitat and their destruction challenges the endangered farmland [[Zhangixalus arvalis|green tree frog]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kuo-fang |first1=Huang |last2=Hsu |first2=Elizabeth |title=Forestry Bureau promotes new strategy to protect endangered tree frog |url=https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202202030001 |website=focustaiwan.tw |date=3 February 2022 |publisher=Focus Taiwan |access-date=4 February 2022}}</ref>

The culms are used for furniture making, but are not suited to construction.<ref name=Mered01/>
